$comment: The provider-neutral SDLC contract. Each $defs entry is 1 shape that a lead, a workflow or a worker writes. It names no provider, model or tool. runtimes.json maps tiers and roles to each provider. check.js validates a value: this shape first, then the meaning. The x- keys are the shared rules that check.js reads. x-first-try: a role named there first spawns at that tier for 1 mechanical step (for the integrator: 1 clean merge), and steps up to its x-roles tier when that try reports a conflict or a red oracle. Tier rule: a task runs at the higher of its planned tier and the tier its brief-writer recommends; a brief may raise the tier, never lower it. The spec step is the one place a tier drops: plan lowers judgment to bounded when the spec leaves nothing uncovered (never lead, never one_way). A scaffold spec test counts as an oracle for the build only: the wave deletes it in its task's merge step. x-need-labels: the issue label of each capability a task may need.

x-tiers.bounded: An oracle covers every behaviour that matters. A tight brief, a file list, the signatures, 15-30 min.
x-tiers.judgment: 1 or more behaviours have no oracle, or the task has a design choice. Also brief-writing, sub-lead, integration and a skeptic.
x-tiers.lead: The plan, the chief of staff, every review, and a change the step-up rule names.

graph.description: A wave: the tasks of 1 parent, their blockers and the base they build on. The plan workflow writes it; the wave workflow reads it.

branch.description: The wave branch that integration pushes to

sha.description: The frozen base. Every task branch starts here or on the wave branch.

fix_lane.description: Default false. When true, one lead-tier fix agent runs on the wave branch for a CRITICAL end-review finding, a convergence-guard major or a red converge gate. It does not count against rework_limit and runs at most once per wave.

task.description: 1 task: 1 outcome, 1 branch, 1 worker. Tasks with no blocker path between them run in parallel, so their files must not overlap.

id.description: Unique in the graph. The issue number as text when the task is 1 issue.

outcome.description: 1 sentence: what is true when the task is done

done_when.description: The checks that prove the outcome, 1 line each

area.description: The area: label of the issue, without the area: prefix

tier.description: The planned tier. The task runs at the higher of this tier and the tier of its brief.

blockers.description: Task ids that must be integrated before this task starts

files.description: The only files the worker may edit

removes.description: Optional: each symbol or path the done-when renames or deletes with no alias left. wave greps each on the target branch before a worker starts. Absent: the check agent reads them from the brief text.

chain.description: The chain of the task. The tasks of 1 chain build on 1 branch, <graph branch>-<chain>, and wait only on tasks of their chain. Tasks in 2 chains may edit the same file. When every chain task has ended, 1 converge step merges the chain branches into the graph branch, in the order each chain first appears in tasks, and runs the gate once. A task with no chain builds on the graph branch; when it waits on a chain task, it starts after the converge. A chain task may also wait on a task with no chain; the chain branch is then cut from the graph branch after that task merges, and that task may not wait on a chain task.

split.description: Part names, x-limits.split_parts_min or more. A sub-lead writes the oracle and 1 brief per part, workers build the parts, an integrator merges them into the task branch.

needs.description: Capabilities from x-capabilities that the task needs. Empty or absent: any agent may take it. An agent takes the task only when its runtime has every one (status enforced or instructed).

one_way.description: True when the task fixes a contract, a save format or a public API that callers depend on and that is costly to reverse. plan runs design-twice for it (2 designs, 1 adversarial judge) and never lowers its tier.

risky.description: True when the plan marks the change risky: a shared file many tasks read, a save or wire format, a public API, a deletion, or behaviour no oracle covers. Absent means false. A risky task gets 1 blast-radius check.

spec_sha.description: The full SHA of the spec commit on spec/<task id>. plan sets it only for a task it spec'd. wave starts the task branch from this SHA, never from a branch name.

resume_from.description: A full SHA, or a branch on the remote, that holds earlier work on the task. wave starts the task branch from it (it wins over spec_sha), merges the wave branch into it, and the worker continues that work.

scaffold.description: The spec tests not marked keep: an oracle for the build only. plan sets it only for a task it spec'd. The integrator deletes those added since the base in the task's merge step, when its checks pass without them.

oracle.description: The proof of a task. files is the inventory of every test or golden file that covers it, read before anyone says what the oracle covers.

uncovered.description: Behaviours no oracle file covers. Not empty means the tier is not bounded. An entry starting with feel: is play feel, proven by a playtest; a task with only such entries gets no spec agent.

reach.description: Optional command template with one {dir} placeholder, for example make unit SYS={dir}. The integrator runs it once for each test folder outside the focused oracle that references a changed file or class name.

brief.description: The output of a brief-writer for 1 task. Its tier is a recommendation: the task runs at the higher of the planned tier and this tier.

removes.description: Each symbol or path the done-when renames or deletes with no alias left. Empty or absent when none. wave greps each on the target branch.

oracle.description: Path of the test or golden file that proves the whole issue

stubs.description: Paths of the stub files committed to the branch

brief.description: Tight brief: outcome, files, the oracle cases this part must pass, what to leave alone

test.description: The command that runs the focused test of this part only

tier.description: judgment when the oracle does not cover the behaviour; lead when the step-up rule applies

escalation.description: Empty when the issue splits cleanly. Otherwise the question for the lead.

task.description: The task id or part name from the brief

sha.description: The full SHA of the last pushed commit

line.description: The last output line of the focused test

red.description: Each failing test that is red on the base too (the wave passes that list), by name as the runner prints it. Only such tests may fail when passed is true

line.description: The last output line of the gate

red.description: Each failing check that is red on the base too, by name as the runner prints it. Only such checks may fail when passed is true

round.description: 0 for the first build, 1 or more for a rework round

escalation.description: Set when status is escalated. Stop and ask; do not guess.

unverified.description: Each test folder or suite you did not run that may use your change. Empty when you ran them all. Do not write 'not verified' in notes instead.

extra_files.description: Every file the worker edited outside its own file list. The integrator checks each against the tasks beside it that are not merged yet.

findings.description: Each problem outside the task that cost the worker time or would break main, classified. Empty or absent when none. The workflow searches the open findings and votes on a match; the worker files nothing.

severity.description: holds only when main would break: a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the command, its last output line, the file

minutes.description: The minutes the problem cost this worker

browser_s.description: Seconds the browser test runs of this agent took; 0 when none

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds this agent waited for a machine-wide browser lock before them; 0 when none

notes.description: 3 lines or fewer. Say what you did not verify.

brief.description: The worker's own short brief when the task came with none: a few lines, the approach, the traps it found, what it did not do.

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

sha.description: The full SHA of the pushed integration branch

skipped.description: Each skipped branch and why, 1 line each

red.description: A wave merge: each failing test of the oracle or the gate that is red on the base too, by name as the runner prints it. Only such tests may fail when oracle_passed is true

reproved.description: A wave merge: false when the merge had no conflict and the merged tree is the tree the worker proved, so only the gate ran; true when the oracle ran again

reworked.description: Parts the sub-lead had to fix

scaffold.description: The scaffold step of a wave merge, after the oracle passed: the scaffold tests deleted, those kept, and the check run without them.

line.description: The last output line, or not run

passed.description: True only when a check ran and passed

base_red.description: A wave merge that is red, but not by the task: kind base when the same check is red on the pre-merge tip too, kind infra when the check could not run (a harness, tool or machine error, not a test result). Empty when the red is the task's.

line.description: Its last output line on the pre-merge tip, or the infra error

tip.description: The full SHA of the pre-merge tip of the target branch

browser_s.description: Seconds the browser test runs of this agent took; 0 when none

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds this agent waited for a machine-wide browser lock before them; 0 when none

closed.description: A wave merge: true when this merge closed the task issue, after the merge was validated and pushed; false when it closed nothing

pruned.description: A wave merge: true when the merged task branch is deleted on the remote and its worktree removed; the converge: each chain branch. Only a branch that is an ancestor of the target

pruned_branch.description: The branches deleted on the remote, space-separated; empty when none

kept.description: Each issue, branch or worktree the close step kept, and why, 1 line each

reach.description: A wave task merge with oracle.reach: each test folder outside the focused oracle that references a changed file or class name, the reach command run for it, and whether it passed. A red not on the base is the task's.

gone.description: A wave task merge: each path the merge deleted or renamed away (git diff --name-status -M: the path of a D line, the old path of an R line), nothing else; empty when none

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

pairs.description: A judgment for each pair of results that solve alike or clash

better.description: The id of the better result, or tie

id.description: A short unique id for the finding

evidence.description: File and line, or the command and its output

cross_issue.description: True when the problem spans 2 or more results

guard.description: true on a major that breaks a convergence guard: a second path, duplicate store or forwarder, or a second mount path

agree.description: True only if you reproduced the problem from the evidence

oracle_list.description: The oracle check before a wave starts: the oracle of each task run in list mode on the commit its branch starts from, then once on the wave base. An oracle that lists and selects 0 tests refuses the graph. A test red on the base is not a task's.

browser_s.description: Seconds the browser test runs of this agent took; 0 when none

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds this agent waited for a machine-wide browser lock before them; 0 when none

listed.description: False when the runner has no list mode; then selected means nothing

selected.description: The count of tests the command selects

red.description: The tests that fail when the oracle runs on the wave base, by name as the runner prints it; empty when all pass

brief_check.description: The check of a brief before a task gets a worker. missing: each asked path of its Files list that is not on the commit its branch starts from nor on its target branch; a missing path sends the task back to a brief-writer. hits: each symbol or path the brief removes, and the files on the target branch that still reference it; a hit outside the task's files, or in an oracle file the task does not own, stops the task for the lead.

missing.description: The asked paths that do not exist; empty when all exist or none was asked

hits.description: 1 entry per removed symbol or path; empty when nothing was asked

files.description: The files on the target branch that contain the symbol; empty when none

remote.description: What an earlier run of the same graph left on the remote, read before a wave starts. wave skips a task whose merge commit is there and resumes a task whose branch is there.

merges.description: The subject of each merge commit since the base on the branches the prompt names, verbatim

heads.description: Each named branch that is on the remote, with its head

queue.description: The ready, claimed issues a flow runs, in the order they start. Each lands in its group branch: 1 per parent issue, named <parent>-<slug>.

group.description: The group branch of the parent: <parent>-<slug>

files.description: The files the task leases from its start to its landing

finding.description: Set when the issue is a queued finding. The flow takes queued findings holds first, then in priority order (x-severity-weights[severity] x votes x minutes, at least 1 minute) in the queue places findings hold; ready issues keep their places.

load.description: The load of the machine before a flow starts an agent: the 1-minute load average and the CPU count.
The 1-minute load average, as uptime prints it

group_pr.description: The ship step of a flow group branch, once every task of its parent has landed: the default branch merged in by a merge commit, the full suite run once on that head, and on green 1 PR into the default branch that closes the parent and merges itself on green. open: the sub-issues of the parent that are still open; any open sub-issue means no PR.

sha.description: The full SHA of the group head the full suite ran on

line.description: The last output line of the full suite, or the merge or harness error

passed.description: True only when the full suite ran and exited 0

pr.description: The URL of the group PR; empty when none was opened

auto_merge.description: True when gh pr merge --auto --merge exited 0 on the PR

open.description: The open sub-issues of the parent, as #N; empty when all are closed

escalation.description: Set when the full suite is red or the merge of the default branch has a conflict

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

landing_review.description: A review of flow landings: a diff review of 1 landing (diff_reviewer tier), or a blind batched review of the last args.review_every landings (reviewer tier). The review files nothing and holds nothing: the flow files or votes each finding, and only a holds finding gets 1 fix agent on its group branch.

landings.description: The task ids of the landings the review read

findings.description: Each problem the review found in those landings, classified. Empty when none.

task.description: The task id of the landing the problem is in; 1 of landings

severity.description: holds only when main would break: a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the file and line, or the command and its last output line

minutes.description: The minutes the problem cost the reviewer; 0 when it cost none

finding.description: 1 classified finding, filed once as an issue with the labels kind:<kind> and sev:<severity>. Before filing, the agent searches the open findings; on a match it votes instead of filing. Priority = x-severity-weights[severity] x votes x minutes (at least 1). Severity holds: main would break (a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working); only holds stops a landing, and it gets 1 fix agent.

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the command, its last output line, the SHA

url.description: The URL of the finding issue, or of the open finding it voted on; empty when the filing failed

minutes.description: The minutes lost to the problem: the filing and every vote, summed

voted.description: True when an open finding matched and the agent voted on it (1 comment naming its task and the minutes lost, and a +1 reaction) instead of filing a new issue

votes.description: The votes on the finding now: 1 for the filing plus 1 per vote comment

blast.description: The output of a blast-radius check: the 1 fact a change is safe because of, and how far it was proven. level: 1 said so, 2 pointed at a file:line, 3 walked the failure step by step, 4 ran code that calls the real function, 5 reproduced in the running app.

target.description: The task id or finding id checked

proof.description: The command and its last output lines. Empty below level 4.

evidence.description: file:line, or the command and its output

cleared.description: What was checked and is fine, 1 line each

critique.description: The output of a completeness critic on a plan: what the tasks and briefs leave out

complete.description: True only when the tasks and briefs cover the whole goal

missing.description: Each gap, 1 line: the behaviour, file, test or decision that no task covers. Empty when complete.

spec.description: The output of a spec agent for 1 task: the spec as code, committed and pushed to its own branch spec/<task id>, cut from the graph base, before the build. The worker cuts its task branch from it. The spec agent owns tests; the worker never edits them.

kind.description: test: a unit or integration test. scene: a scripted scene run whose exit code or log is checked (for example a Godot 4 headless run with scripted input). golden: a golden output the command compares.

tests.description: Paths of the failing tests, scene scripts or golden files. They become oracle files.

keep.description: The tests that meet the keep rule (AGENTS-AND-MODELS.md, Tests), and every test the spec amended. Each is in tests. Every other test is scaffold: an oracle for the build only, deleted by the wave.

created.description: The spec tests this spec created: not in the tree at the graph base. A test not in created was there before and is keep.

stubs.description: Paths of the stub files the worker fills in. Each is inside the task files.

sketch.description: The caller usage sketch: 5 to 15 lines of how a caller uses the signatures

command.description: The focused command. It runs the old oracle and the new spec tests.

line.description: The last output line of the command before the build

failed.description: True: the command failed before the build, for the intended reason

uncovered.description: Behaviours the old oracle and the spec still do not pin. Empty: the task may become bounded. An entry starting with feel: is play feel, proven by a playtest; a task with only such entries gets no spec agent.

sha.description: The full SHA of the pushed spec commit

gate.description: Present when the plan has a gate. The repo gate run on the spec commit. passed is true when the gate is green, or when its only red is the failing asserts of the spec tests themselves; false when any other check is red (a lint, comment budget, format or type check on the stubs or spec tests) and you could not fix it.

line.description: The last output line of the gate when passed is false

notes.description: 3 lines or fewer. Say what you did not verify.

design.description: 1 design of a one-way task: signatures and a usage sketch, no files written

pick.description: The verdict of an adversarial judge on 2 designs

flaws_a.description: How a caller misuses design a, or a later change breaks it

claim.description: Who owns a task. The record is an issue comment: the first line is agentic-sdlc:claim, then this object as a JSON code block. (1) The owner is the earliest claimed comment that no later released comment of the same lead cancels and no later claim supersedes. The comment's server created_at gives the order; the client field at never decides. (2) After a lead posts a claim, it reads the comments again before its first push; if it does not own the task, it posts released and stops. (3) A claim is stale when its created_at and the last commit time of the remote branch are both older than x-limits.stale_claim_minutes. (4) A new lead takes over only a stale claim: it posts a claim with supersedes and resume_sha (the remote branch head) and resumes from that SHA. If the branch is not on the remote (the old lead died before its first push), resume_sha is base_sha and only the age of the claim comment decides. (5) Every lead fetches the branch and reads the comments again before every push; it stops when a later claim supersedes it. (6) When the remote head is not a descendant of resume_sha or of the lead's own last push, someone rewrote the branch: stop and escalate.

lead.description: A stable id of the lead session

at.description: Client time, for people. The comment's created_at decides order and staleness.

supersedes.description: The URL of the stale claim comment this claim replaces

resume_sha.description: The remote branch head the new lead resumes from

claim_comment.description: 1 claim comment as the lead reads it from the issue, with the server time. The host is any GitHub host: github.com or a GitHub Enterprise Server host.

created_at.description: GitHub's created_at. It decides order and staleness.

transition.description: 1 phase change of 1 task. x-transitions lists the allowed changes. A task is integrated before it is reviewed: the batched review runs beside the build, off the critical path, and a rework round lands as a new integration.

metrics.description: 1 report row per task. A runtime that cannot measure tokens or cost writes unavailable; it never writes 0.

model.description: The model the runtime spawned, as the runtime names it

agents.description: Every agent the task started: brief, build, review share, rework

elapsed_s.description: Lead clock, from claim to integration

closed_at.description: Set when a validated merge closed the task issue and pruned its branch: the at of that merge report

pruned.description: true when the task branch and worktree are deleted; needs closed_at or reopened

reopened.description: true when the task issue closed at a validated merge and reopened because the task did not end merged; closed_at is then absent

browser_s.description: Seconds of browser test runs, summed over the reports of the task's agents

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds the task's agents waited for a machine-wide browser lock, summed over their reports

reproved.description: Set when the task merged: true when a merge of the task ran its oracle again, false when each merge kept the worker's proof

runtime.description: The facts of 1 provider. A key of runtimes.json. The workflows take it as args.runtime. It has no field outside these properties: the evidence strings hold each fact and its proof.

tiers.description: Each tier to the model and effort this provider spawns

worktree_root.description: Repo-relative directory of task worktrees. Each runtime has its own root, so 2 runtimes never share a worktree directory.

agent_types.description: Each role in x-roles to the agent type name of this provider

concurrency.description: Most agents at once. null: the harness decides.

capabilities.description: Each name in x-capabilities to its status and evidence. A name in x-optional-capabilities may be left out; a runtime that leaves it out does not have it.

verified.description: False: the model id or effort is a guess. check.js lists it.

status.description: enforced: the runtime refuses a breach. instructed: only the prompt asks for it.
